answer: The sable multiplier is published, charged in pulse, and bridge lists each payment. A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, as the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 8 for each account already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 882 identities would post 1719 proofs and burn roughly 20 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
